notes: §1985:XVI.3.3.3 SRL2.2: a MERGE in an independent segment names an output procedure totally within non-independent segments or "Wholly within the same independent segment as that MERGE statement". SortBinder.CheckSegmentation sends the OUTPUT PROCEDURE range to Segmentation.CheckProcedures (asked only at COBOL-85, where segment-numbers exist); RangeAllowed returns true for a single independent segment only when it equals the MERGE's own segment (only == from) and never for a fixed and independent mix, else COBOL6877. Probes at --std 85 (classes b,c,e,f): MERGE in 60 with output in 60, in 20 THRU 30 and in 60 THRU 60 compile and run (four merged records); MERGE in 50 with output 50 THRU 50 runs; MERGE in 60 naming 70 (the witness), 60 THRU 20, and MERGE in 99 naming 50 refused COBOL6877; at --std 2023 the segment-numbers are refused COBOL0902. Which procedures count is docs/CONFORMANCE.md's determination: the ones the MERGE names, not their PERFORM closure (CCVS-85 SG102A/SG103A).

next.reason: 1985: "Wholly within the same independent segment as that MERGE statement."; 2023: "No 2023 clause holds the Segmentation feature (independent segments); no candidate states this restriction.". The rule restricts MERGE procedures to independent segments of the Segmentation module. No 2023 clause holds that feature, and no candidate covers segments or this restriction.
